thought.text: The BFS shows MainPage.vue's chain is clean (only a **type-only** import of the missing `Sensor`, which Vite strips — note the path resolves to `resources/types/Sensor.ts`, confirming `../../` from `js/pages/`). Now let me confirm: (1) the transformed `app.ts` globs which pages (does it include the broken Dashboard.vue), and (2) the broken chain only affects Dashboard.

reasoning_content:
My BFS is showing `resources/types/Sensor.ts` as reachable, which is odd—it looks like the `../../types/Sensor` import got normalized to a path outside resources/js. The issue is that `../../` from `resources/js/pages/` should land in `resources/types/Sensor`, but that doesn't match the actual types directory at `resources/js/types/`.

So the real problem is that `../../types/Sensor` resolves to `resources/types/Sensor.ts`, which doesn't exist—it's a type-only import that Vite strips away, so Vite doesn't care, but it's still broken from the build's perspective. The BFS is incorrectly reporting `resources/types/Sensor.ts` as reachable because it's treating it as a resolved file rather than catching that it doesn't actually exist.

Now looking at the MainPage chain: Navigation, Sensor, Ochsi, HomeInfoCard, InfoCard, and SensorCard are all reachable and complete, with only a type-only import to the missing Sensor type (which gets stripped) and an external `@inertiajs/vue3` dependency that exists in node_modules. So MainPage should render fine in dev mode. I'm trying to verify whether Navigation.vue, Sensor.vue, and Ochsi.vue have any other missing imports besides the type-only `Sensor` reference—my BFS found no other value-imports missing from them. But I'm puzzled because Navigation.vue imports `../../types/Sensor` from `resources/js/components/`, which resolves to `resources/types/Sensor.ts`, which doesn't exist. I need to figure out why this isn't causing a build failure.

Since it's a type-only import, Vite's Vue SFC compiler strips it out, so the build never actually tries to resolve it. That's why the build failed on `UserMenuContent` before it ever got to these files—they're stripped before resolution. The dev server would handle this the same way: esbuild strips `import { Sensor } from '../../types/Sensor'` because it's type-only, so Vite doesn't need to resolve it. Let me quickly test the Vite transform for Navigation.vue and the MainPage chain components to confirm they all transform without errors, then fetch the full HomePage to see what the browser would actually load. I'm also going to check the app.ts glob to see if Dashboard.vue is included, which would pull in AppLayout and the missing NavUser/UserInfo/AppHeader chain.

action.command: cd /workspace && echo "=== glob in transformed app.ts (which pages registered) ==="; curl -s "http://localhost:5173/resources/js/app.ts" | grep -oE "import\(.*/pages/[^)]+\.vue" | head; echo; echo "=== Confirm NavUser/AppHeader transform (should be broken) ==="; for f in NavUser AppHeader; do echo "-- $f --"; curl -s "http://localhost:5173/resources/js/components/$f.vue" | grep -oE "\"message\":\"[^\"]+\"" | head -1; done; echo; echo "=== Confirm MainPage + its comps transform OK (200 & no Error) ==="; for f in "pages/MainPage" "components/Navigation" "components/Sensor" "components/Ochsi" "components/HomeInfoCard" "components/InfoCard" "components/SensorCard"; do code=$(curl -s -o /tmp/r.txt -w "%{http_code}" "http://localhost:5173/resources/js/$f.vue"); err=$(grep -c "Failed to resolve" /tmp/r.txt); echo "$f -> HTTP $code, resolve-errors=$err"; done
